column5: Iceland lands far more fish than its people eat and exports most of it.
Mauritania's waters are fished mostly for export (fishmeal, frozen fish).
Namibia exports most of its hake and horse-mackerel catch.
Ecuador is a large exporter of shrimp and tuna.
The Seychelles land and can tuna mostly for export.
Ghana is the world's second cocoa producer and grinds or exports almost all of it.
New Zealand sells abroad almost all of its milk, as milk powder, butter and cheese.
Nicaragua exports most of its coffee.

FAO's balance has Botswana re-selling about 230 kt of the 860 kt of maize it buys a year (likely maize meal and feed to its neighbours), which the trade records do not show. Its cereal self-sufficiency is about a tenth either way (12.9% as published, about 9% without those exports).
